_about: Airspace hazards for flight routing (air_route.py). CURATED BY HAND: every zone carries the bulletin it comes from, its revision date and the date it lapses. THIS FILE MUST BE KEPT CURRENT — EASA revises CZIBs every few weeks during an active conflict (the Middle East set was revised on 2026-09-30, Saudi Arabia on 2026-10-09). air_route.py flags a zone whose valid_until has passed and the whole file once `reviewed` is older than `review_every_days`. Check https://www.easa.europa.eu/en/domains/air-operations/czibs and https://www.faa.gov/air_traffic/publications/us_restrictions/ and update the dates.
geometry_note: Zones are drawn from country outlines (backend/geo/countries.geojson) as an approximation of the FIR: a FIR also covers territorial and some international waters, and a few bulletins restrict only part of a FIR along waypoint lines that are not geocoded here (named in `geometry_caveat`).

zones.name: Iran (FIR Tehran OIIX)
zones.why: EASA: "Not operate within the airspace of Iran, FIR Tehran (OIIX), at all altitudes and flight levels."

sources.note: standing US prohibition; faa.gov refused the automated check on 2026-10-12 — verify the current NOTAM

zones.name: Iraq (FIR Baghdad ORBB)
zones.why: EASA: "Not operate within the airspace of Iraq, FIR Baghdad (ORBB), at all altitudes and flight levels."

sources.note: standing US prohibition; verify the current NOTAM

zones.name: Persian Gulf waters (FIRs Bahrain, Kuwait, Doha, Emirates)
zones.geometry_caveat: a hand-drawn outline of the Gulf waters; it includes Bahrain and Qatar, over which the bulletin says only "exercise caution"
zones.why: EASA: "Not operate at all altitudes and flight levels within the airspace over the waters of the Persian Gulf" — except as needed to arrive at or depart from aerodromes in those FIRs; caution over land.

zones.name: Gulf of Oman west of 58°E (FIR Muscat)
zones.geometry_caveat: hand-drawn outline of the waters west of 58°E
zones.why: EASA: do not operate at any altitude over the waters of the Gulf of Oman west of 58°E (FIR Muscat); caution over land.

zones.name: Saudi Arabia (FIR Jeddah OEJD)
zones.geometry_caveat: the no-operate portions are bounded by RIBOK–BOSUT–MIGDA–RAGNO–MIXUG–DEKLO–OBSAM–SILPA and ULBAM–TOTEB–DURMA–LAKSO–SOLAT, which are not geocoded here: the whole country is drawn at a caution weight instead
zones.why: EASA: "Not operate, at all flight levels and altitudes, within the portions of the airspace of Saudi Arabia" defined in the bulletin; exercise caution in the rest of FIR Jeddah.

zones.name: Jordan (FIR Amman OJAC)
zones.why: EASA: "Not operate within the airspace of Jordan, FIR Amman (OJAC), at all altitudes and flight levels."

zones.name: Lebanon (FIR Beirut OLBB)
zones.why: EASA: "Not operate within the airspace of Lebanon at all altitudes and flight levels" — Beirut (OLBA) only with an approach from / departure over the sea and a current risk assessment.

zones.name: Syria (FIR Damascus OSTT)
zones.geometry_caveat: all altitudes west of ZELAF–BASEM–LOTAX–LATEB, below FL260 east of it; the line is not geocoded, so the whole country is drawn at all altitudes
zones.why: EASA: "Not operate at all flight levels and altitudes, west of the line connecting ZELAF – BASEM – LOTAX – LATEB" and "Not operate below FL 260 in the remainder of the FIR Damascus".

zones.name: Ukraine (FIRs Lviv, Kyiv, Dnipro, Simferopol, Odesa)
zones.why: EASA: "Operators should not operate within the aforementioned airspace" — FIRs UKLV, UKBV, UKBU, UKDV, UKFV, UKOV, all altitudes.

sources.ref: SFAR 113 (14 CFR part 91) — Simferopol and Dnipropetrovsk FIRs; KICZ NOTAM for the rest of Ukraine

zones.name: Russia west of 60°E (FIRs Moscow, Rostov, St Petersburg, Samara, Yekaterinburg)
zones.geometry_caveat: Kaliningrad (not named in the bulletin) is left out
zones.why: EASA "recommends not to operate within the affected airspace of the Russian Federation located west of longitude 60° East" at all altitudes and flight levels.

zones.name: Belarus (FIR Minsk UMMV)
zones.why: EASA Safety Directives SD-2021-02 and SD-2021-03 prohibit EU operators from FIR Minsk (named in CZIB-2022-01R14).

zones.name: Sudan (FIR Khartoum HSSS)
zones.why: EASA "recommends not to fly within the airspace over Sudan at all altitudes and flight levels."

zones.name: Libya (FIR Tripoli HLLL)
zones.why: EASA: "Not operate within the airspace of Libya (FIR Tripoli - HLLL) below FL 320"; exercise caution above it.

zones.name: Yemen (FIR Sana'a OYSC)
zones.geometry_caveat: the maritime routes east of B400, where the bulletin asks only for caution, are outside the land outline drawn here
zones.why: EASA: "Not operate in the airspace of Yemen, Sana'a FIR, at all altitudes and flight levels."

zones.name: Afghanistan (FIR Kabul OAKX)
zones.why: EASA: "Not operate within the airspace of Afghanistan (FIR Kabul - OAKX) below FL 320."

zones.name: Pakistan — Baluchistan and Khyber Pakhtunkhwa
zones.geometry_caveat: the two provinces are approximated as Pakistan west of 71.6°E, which also takes in parts of Sindh and Punjab
zones.why: EASA: "Not operate in the airspace of Pakistan, FIR Karachi (OPKR) and FIR Lahore (OPLR)" below FL260 over Baluchistan and Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.

zones.name: Mali (FIRs Niamey DRRR, Dakar GOOO)
zones.why: EASA: "Not operate in FIR Niamey (DRRR) and FIR Dakar (GOOO) within the territory and airspace of Mali below FL260."

zones.name: Somalia (FIR Mogadishu HCSM)
zones.why: EASA: "Not operate in the airspace of Somalia at or below FL 260."

zones.name: North Korea (FIR Pyongyang ZKKP)
zones.why: FAA SFAR 79 prohibits US operators in the Pyongyang FIR west of 132°E; unannounced missile launches. (EASA's CZIB-2017-06R2 was withdrawn.)

sam_envelopes.name: Kaliningrad S-400 envelope
sam_envelopes.why: S-400 (SA-21) batteries are based in the Kaliningrad exclave; the 48N6 interceptor is credited with about 250 km (the 40N6, up to 380–400 km). Civil traffic over the Baltic transits routinely: drawn as a low, standing weight so its overlap with the Baltic GPS jamming is visible, not as a no-fly recommendation.

sources.ref: The Military Balance (Russia — Western Military District)

event_rules._about: Missile / air-defence activity from this app's own events (GeoConfirmed `air` category and keyword classes, open alerts) becomes a decaying zone. Radii are deliberately conservative (larger than the weapon's reach at airliner altitudes) because an engagement area is wider than its geolocated point; precedents: MH17 (Buk, 17 Jul 2014, FL330), PS752 (Tor-M1, Tehran, 8 Jan 2020, during retaliatory missile strikes), AZAL 8243 (Russian air defence over Grozny during a drone attack, 25 Dec 2024).

air_defence.label: Air-defence activity
air_defence.why: Air defences were engaging here: airliners have been shot down in exactly this situation (PS752, AZAL 8243).

missile.label: Missile / long-range drone strikes
missile.why: Missile or long-range drone strikes draw air-defence fire across the whole area, at all altitudes.

airstrike.label: Airstrikes
airstrike.why: Military aircraft releasing weapons here; the area is contested by air defences.

ucdp.why: Ground conflict baseline (UCDP): MANPADS and light anti-aircraft fire reach about FL150 — relevant to climb and descent, barely to cruise. UCDP lags about three months, so this is a baseline, never news.

gps.why: Aircraft here lost or degraded their satellite fix (ADS-B NIC/NACp) — jamming or spoofing: a navigation and terrain-warning hazard, not a shoot-down risk.

openaip.why: Prohibited airspace from openAIP (only the viewports already cached on disk), counted when it reaches above FL190. Restricted (R) areas are left out: most are military training areas activated by NOTAM, which are not modelled here.
